metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

metadata.summary: Background: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) followed by a reperfusion results in a phasic response by cardiac macrophages. During the first 7 days after AMI, macrophage populations exhibit dynamic phenotypic changes. Ultimately, inflammatory damage results in ventricular remodeling and fibrosis. Macrophages are critical to cardiac function and long-term prognoses. Objective: Elucidate the spatiotemporal behavior of specific macrophage subtypes during  AMI and identify novel genes with prospective therapeutic potential. Methods: We implement an IRI mouse model of AMI to assess cardiac macrophage behavior during AMI. RCM were isolated using flow cytometry and analyzed with NanoString. Pathway enrichment analysis annotated statistically significant genes. We employed transcriptome-wide, spatiotemporal analysis of cardiac tissue samples during  AMI.

metadata.summary: Microexons are extremely short exons that are highly conserved in vertebrates and are essential for normal brain development. Their small size poses a challenge for canonical exon-definition splice site recognition, which typically relies on spliceosomal interactions across standard length exons. Here, we determine the sequence and RNA structural features of neural microexons in humans in comparison with chickens. We find that neural microexons share intronic features that extend the functional distance between the branchpoint and the 3’ splice site, including distal positioning and lengthening of polypyrimidine tracts. Using experimental RNA structure-probing on a subset of neural microexons, we show that the branchpoint-to-splice site region is unusually accessible and relatively unpaired compared to other exon classes. However, we find little support for shared RNA secondary structures between orthologous human and chicken precursor RNAs despite high sequence conservation. Using the chick embryo as a developmental model, we demonstrate that a subset of neural microexons undergo dynamic, stage-specific regulation during brain development that correlates with expression of known microexon regulators, SRRM4 and NOVA1. Our data suggest that neural microexon splicing fluctuates during brain development and may rely on an extended polypyrimidine tract and structural accessibility for splicing efficiency, rather than conserved secondary structures.

observations.text: The incidence of the vast majority of neurodegenerative, cancer, and metabolic diseases generally increases exponentially with age. In large-scale biobanks, linking time-to-diagnosis information in electronic health records to multiple genomic (``multiomics'') measures has the potential to reveal the genes and biological pathways involved in the disease onset and progression. To date, association testing has commonly been conducted by testing one variable at a time using semiparametric Cox proportional hazards (CoxPH) models, which ignores correlation structure and increases the risk of false discoveries. To address these issues, we introduce a novel fully parametric Bayesian computational method, vampW, based on the Vector Approximate Message Passing framework applied to a Weibull model. vampW jointly models correlated features, while providing an interpretable hazard structure, producing a continuous survival curve, and incorporating prior knowledge. In an extensive simulation study, we demonstrate that joint modeling of omics data and time-to-event outcomes with vampW, substantially reduces false discoveries in comparison to marginal testing and other forms of joint CoxPH models. In 53,018 individuals from the UK Biobank, vampW identifies 219 protein associations with 24 disease outcomes, most of which are not among the top marginal discoveries. We further correct protein levels for exponential age effects, identifying 1,308 associations and highlighting the sensitivity of the analysis to age-correction methodology. Our findings replicate in independent cohorts using different measurement technologies, within data from Iceland and a novel Generation Scotland proteomics dataset. vampW also achieves significant improvement in the prediction of disease onset times: across 14 outcomes, it reduces the root mean squared error by over 30% and 26%, when compared to CoxPH variants and the deep learning approach DeepSurv, respectively, while maintaining predictive utility in minority populations. In summary, vampW offers accurate and interpretable variable selection and out-of-sample prediction within a single computational framework, making it a powerful tool for dissecting the genomic architecture of common complex disease onset.
observations.title: Joint Variable Selection for Omic Biomarkers in Time-to-Event Data

metadata.summary: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on a combination of canonical cardiac transcription factors, typically consisting of Mef2c, Gata4, and Tbx5 (MGT). However, successful lineage conversion requires additional endogenous factors that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional changes underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (Atf7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss of function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0–3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while derepressing fibroblast  and extracellular matrix–associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non reprogrammed state. These findings support a bifunctional regulatory role of Atf7 in promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation while repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks.

metadata.summary: Myocardial infarction (MI) causes cardiomyocyte loss and fibrotic scar formation, disrupting electrical communication and impairing cardiac function. Conductive hydrogels have been studied to reconstruct an electroactive microenvironment for the infarcted myocardium, yet their regenerative effect is limited by the impaired function of surviving cardiomyocytes. Here, we developed a mechanoelectrically active and paintable hydrogel capable of converting cardiac motion into localized electrical stimulation to repair infarcted myocardium. The paintable nature of the hydrogel enables easy application onto irregular epicardial surfaces using a customized brush, while subsequent photocrosslinking allows selective adhesion of the hydrogel to only epicardial surfaces, not to surrounding tissues. Under cyclic loading and in contracting cardiac organoids, the hydrogel generated physiologically relevant electrical potentials, demonstrating efficient deformation-induced charge generation. In a rat MI model, the hydrogel providing electrostimulation alleviated ventricular wall thinning and fibrosis, promoted neovascularization and M2 macrophage polarization, and improved cardiac function. Transcriptomic analysis further revealed upregulation of genes involved in myocardial contraction and energy metabolism. As such, our study offers a minimally invasive and clinically translatable approach for cardiac repair and other tissue applications.

metadata.summary: Ponatinib is a potent tyrosine kinase inhibitor and primarily used in the treatment of chronic myelogenous leukemia and Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Due to the potential vascular side effects including cardiotoxicity (CTX), its broad anti-cancer capability is restricted, while replaceable better alternative is currently not available. Investigating ponatinib CTX is for getting a better understanding of the fundamental molecular mechanisms which are crucial for developing innovative cardiovascular protection. We have established a ponatinib-induced CTX mouse model, specifically, evaluated long-term effects of ponatinib on cardiac structural and function and demonstrated cardioprotective effects in inducible cardiomyocyte-specific ROCK1 and ROCK2 knockout mouse hearts (DKO). To explore the mechanisms underlying the cardioprotective effects in DKO hearts, single nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) study has been implemented.  Results have revealed that double ROCK deletion in cardiomyocytes mitigates ponatinib-induced CTX through suppressing pathological remodeling of cardiomyocytes and nonmyocytes.

observations.text: Acetylcholine and dopamine significantly modulate striatal circuits and are essential for reward learning and action selection. Cholinergic interneurons can locally trigger dopamine release through beta2-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors expressed on dopamine axons1-3. However, the causal contribution of this local cholinergic control of dopamine to behaviour and striatal output remains unresolved, with recent studies reaching contrasting conclusions about the extent and behavioural relevance of local acetylcholine-dopamine coupling4-6. Here, to directly test the causal contribution of this pathway, we conditionally deleted beta2-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptors from midbrain neurons in adult mice. This manipulation selectively abolished cholinergic interneuron-evoked dopamine release in the striatum. In a reward-based instrumental task, mice lacking this pathway showed decrements in effort that depended on the reinforcement context, and failed to adjust actions in a choice task when effort and reward costs varied. Substantia nigra beta2-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptor deletion also markedly weakened cholinergic interneuron-mediated disynaptic inhibition of striatal projection neurons, showing that disruption of beta2-dependent cholinergic control of dopamine alters how cholinergic activity is transmitted to striatal output. Together, these findings establish the importance of local acetylcholine-dopamine coupling for regulating striatal output and influencing whether actions are sustained and adjusted as effort, reward, and outcomes change.
observations.title: Nicotinic control of dopamine release shapes striatal output and engages adaptive action selection.

metadata.summary: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture is a major cause of myocardial infarction and stroke. However, the precise drivers of plaque destabilisation remain elusive. We hypothesised that antigen-driven, autoimmune-like T cell responses are central to the destabilisation and rupture of atherosclerotic plaques. To dissect T cell responses specifically in unstable compared to stable plaques, we leveraged near-infrared autofluorescence (NIRAF) imaging-guided dissection of human carotid plaques and our tandem stenosis model in mice. We applied single-cell multi-omics to study T cell differentiation states and T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires. T cell responses in unstable versus stable atherosclerosis were distinct. Unstable human plaques contained highly expanded, autoimmune-like CD8+ T cells with markedly increased cytotoxic signatures, reduced exhaustion and distinct clonal repertoires compared to stable regions. Most plaque CD8+ T cells exhibited a pronounced tissue-resident transcriptional program. Autoimmune-like cytotoxic and tissue-resident CD8+ T cell responses were also evident in murine atherosclerosis, where restricting the activation of antigen-driven CD8+ T cells prevented plaque destabilisation.

observations.text: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) coupled with Dorado modification-aware basecalling enables mapping of epitranscriptomic modifications including N6-methyladenosine (m6A) at the level of individual RNAs. However, the sensitivity, specificity, and reproducibility of this method remain unclear and have only recently begun to be addressed through systematic benchmarking studies. Here, we aimed to establish a best-practice workflow for DRS-based epitranscriptomic analyses. Specifically, we evaluated multiple Dorado versions and models using RNA isolated from primary cells and unmodified in vitro transcribed RNAs. We further utilized an m6A methyltransferase inhibitor as a specificity control. We established that stringent filtering is necessary to reduce the contribution of background and found that Dorado predictions captured an increasing proportion of GLORI sites detected at high m6A/A proportions. Further, by applying DRS to a human primary fibroblast and a HD10.6 neuron dataset, we detected differences in the predicted m6A/A proportions at conserved sites between these datasets. Our study thus presents the first systematic comparison of Dorado and GLORI from the same input RNA and expands characterization of the m6A epitranscriptome to fibroblasts and neurons.

observations.text: Predicting implantation outcomes in vitro fertilization (IVF) is challenging because clinically relevant information becomes available at different points during treatment. In this study, we developed a stage-aware, leakage-conscious, and explainable machine-learning framework to predict implantation using a public IVF dataset. {beta}-HCG was excluded to avoid potential downstream target leakage. The data were divided into training, validation, and independent test sets. Several machine-learning models, including Logistic Regression, Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees, XGBoost, and Hist Gradient Boosting, were optimized using stratified cross-validation. A fixed RF model was then evaluated at three stages of the IVF process, using baseline couple characteristics, gamete and fertilization variables, and embryological variables, respectively. Model performance improved as additional treatment-related information became available, with the largest improvement observed after the inclusion of embryological variables. The final RF model showed good predictive performance on the independent test set. The number of embryos was consistently identified as the most important predictor across RF, permutation, and SHAP analyses. Overall, the findings suggest that IVF implantation prediction becomes more accurate as later-stage treatment information is incorporated, particularly information related to embryological characteristics. The proposed approach also provides interpretable predictions while reducing the risk of information leakage. Further evaluation using independent clinical datasets is needed before the framework can be considered for clinical use.
observations.title: Stage-Aware and Explainable Machine Learning for Predicting IVF Implantation

metadata.summary: Non-infectious granulomatous diseases, including sarcoidosis, lack targeted, steroid-sparing therapies to disrupt the persistent immune cell aggregates that drive chronic tissue morbidity. Integrating multi-organ single-cell RNA sequencing with spatial transcriptomics, we identify conserved macrophage-specific induction of osteopontin (OPN) across human skin, lung, and heart lesions. Mechanistically, we show that local tissue coagulation acts as a functional checkpoint, where proteolytic cleavage of OPN by tissue thrombin generates OPN fragments that activate macrophages through α4 integrin, which amplifies macrophage OPN expression and establishes a feed-forward circuit that sustains granuloma stability. In mouse models, genetic or pharmacologic disruption of this coagulation-immune axis, including the repurposed direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran and thrombin cleavage-blocking OPN antibodies, reduces granuloma formation and promotes resolution of established chronic lesions. Together, these findings identify a thrombin-dependent feed-forward coagulation–immune circuit that maintains granuloma stability and provides multiple therapeutically actionable targets for non-infectious granulomatous disease.

metadata.summary: Myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury triggers the recruitment of inflammatory cells, including neutrophils and monocytes. Currently, effective treatment strategies are not available for this widely occurring harmful condition. Using metabololipidomics, we uncovered relative reductions in the pro-resolving lipid mediator Resolvin-D1 (RvD1) early after reperfusion in both mouse and human transplanted hearts, and that exogenous treatment led to elevated tissue levels of RvD1. By intravital two-photon microscopy, we discovered that that pre-operative instillation of RvD1 into the donor heart or peri-operative systemic recipient RvD1 treatment reduced recruitment of neutrophils. Mechanistically, we found that RvD1 provides protection by signaling through Alx/Fpr2 on donor monocytes, which reduces their production of IL-1b, attenuating intravascular neutrophil aggregation and extravasation.  After allogeneic transplantation, peri-operative RvD1 treatment reduces myeloid cell recruitment, abrogates macrophage pro-inflammatory signaling within cardiac allografts, and significantly prolongs graft survival. This study defines the mechanistic basis of a therapeutic strategy that modulates inflammatory responses during myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury and provides a platform for the design of clinical trials.

observations.text: Whilst forms of non-associative learning such as habituation are widely reported in single-celled organisms, whether associative learning is possible in systems without a nervous system is contested. In this study, we implemented a conditioning paradigm in the acellular slime mould Physarum polycephalum through repeated pairings of nutrients with an aversive blue light stimulus. We first established that blue light is aversive under our conditioning protocol, slowing migration and producing broader, less directed growth, confirming its well documented effect on behaviour. Subjects were then trained in up to four training sessions by placing an oat stimulus inside a region with blue light before testing with the light presented alone. Trained subjects were more likely to reach the blue light region compared to untrained controls, with shorter latency, suggesting that Physarum weakens its avoidance of blue light after the region has repeatedly coincided with a nutrient. However, engagement did not strengthen with additional pairings, a pattern that admits multiple competing explanations in which associative and non-associative processes plausibly contribute to more transient associative-like effects. We conclude that a history of co-presentation is sufficient to relax an aversive response in Physarum but cannot, within the present study, attribute that change to associative learning.

metadata.summary: The molecular and cellular processes leading to aortic aneurysm development in Marfan syndrome (MFS) remain poorly understood. We examined the changes of aortic cell populations and gene expression in MFS. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA seq) on ascending aortic aneurysm tissues from patients with MFS (n=3) and age-matched non-aneurysmal control tissues from cardiac donors and recipients (n=4). The expression of key molecules was confirmed by immunostaining. Diverse populations of smooth muscle cells (SMCs), fibroblasts, and endothelial cell (EC) were detected in the aortic wall. Aortic tissues from MFS showed alterations of cell populations with increased de-differentiated proliferative SMCs compared to controls. Furthermore, there was a downregulation of MYOCD and MYH11 in SMCs, and an upregulation of COL1A1/2 in fibroblasts in MFS samples compared to controls. We also examined TGF-β signaling, an important pathway in aortic homeostasis. We found that TGFB1 was significantly upregulated in two fibroblast clusters in MFS tissues. However, TGF-β receptor genes (predominantly TGFBR2) and SMAD genes were downregulated in SMCs, fibroblasts, and ECs, indicating impairment in TGF-β signaling in MFS. Despite upregulation of TGFB1, the rest of the canonical TGF-β pathway was consistently downregulated in MFS, indicating a potential compromise of TGF-β signaling and lack of stimulus for SMC differentiation.

observations.text:
BackgroundComparing long-term outcomes of gastric cancer surgery between hospitals requires a common reference. Risk-adjusted benchmarks depend on the model and population used to build them and are difficult for another hospital to reproduce. TNM stage is a prognostic classification already recorded for every resected gastric cancer. We report unadjusted stage-specific overall survival from a consecutive cohort with complete follow-up as reference data and propose a minimal dataset for producing comparable figures elsewhere.

MethodsThe cohort comprised 690 consecutive eligible patients who underwent curative-intent D2 gastrectomy for stage I to III adenocarcinoma at Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai, in 2019. All operations were performed by eight experienced, high-volume consultant surgeons. Stage followed the AJCC 8th edition: pTNM after upfront surgery (n = 570) and ypTNM after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (n = 120). Overall survival was estimated by the Kaplan-Meier method without adjustment.

ResultsThere were 199 deaths, 181 within five years. Every survivor was followed for at least 68.1 months. After upfront surgery, five-year overall survival was 95.0% (95% CI 91.4 to 97.1) for stage I, 83.8% (76.5 to 89.0) for stage II and 56.5% (49.2 to 63.1) for stage III, and was 95.0% in IA and 95.2% in IB, falling to 26.7% in IIIC. After neoadjuvant chemotherapy, five-year survival was 78.6%, 61.9% and 31.3% for ypStage I, II and III. Pooling pTNM and ypTNM lowered stage III five-year survival to 50.2%. The proposed minimal dataset has 16 items, 13 of them recorded during the admission for gastrectomy.

ConclusionsThese figures are intended as a reference for comparing hospitals rather than as a standard of care. We propose 16 items, most of them routinely recorded, from which another hospital can produce the same table and compare its results by stage.
observations.title: Stage-specific overall survival with complete five-year follow-up after D2 gastrectomy for gastric cancer at a referral hospital in Shanghai, China: a reference for comparing hospitals

metadata.summary: Background: Direct reprogramming of cardiac fibroblasts (CFs) into induced cardiomyocytes (iCMs) holds promise as a therapeutic strategy for heart regeneration. Post-myocardial infarction (MI), resident quiescent CFs (QCFs) activate and differentiate into myofibroblasts (MFs) in the infarcted region that drive pathological cardiac fibrosis. Converting these injury-activated MFs into iCMs could simultaneously alleviate fibrosis and replenish lost cardiomyocytes. However, whether the marked heterogeneity of CFs in the infarcted heart—and in particular the activation of QCFs into MFs—creates an intrinsic barrier that limits the reprogramming of these injury-activated MFs remains unknown. Methods: To define the molecular basis of this heterogeneity, we purified PDGFRα⁺ cardiac fibroblasts and used Postn lineage tracing to distinguish injury-activated MFs from quiescent CFs, enabling matched comparison of their reprogramming competence and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) profiling of post-MI CF subpopulations. A targeted in vitro shRNA screen was conducted against 9 MF-enriched TFs as candidate molecular barriers for cardiac reprogramming. The lead candidate was validated in mouse MFs, QCFs, human iPSC-derived MFs, primary human cardiac fibroblasts, and in vivo using dual-recombinase-mediated lineage tracing. Mechanistic insights were gained through integrated bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq and Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag), together with functional assays including DNA-binding–deficient and domain-swap MEOX1 mutants. Results: We identified the upregulated transcription factor MEOX1—a known fibrosis determinant downstream of the key post-MI cytokines TGF-β1 and IL-1β—as the principal molecular barrier responsible for the profound reprogramming resistance of MFs. MEOX1 knockdown markedly enhanced reprogramming efficiency in both mouse and human MFs and enabled GATA4-free reprogramming combinations. This inhibition depended on MEOX1’s transcriptional activation activity, as disrupting its DNA-binding domain or fusing it to a repressor domain rescued reprogramming. Integrated scRNA-seq and CUT&Tag analyses revealed that MEOX1 binds and stabilizes a fibrotic, MF-defining transcriptional program that antagonizes the cardiogenic program, while also modulating the inflammatory response; its knockdown disrupted this fibrotic network to favor iCM fate acquisition. Using stringent dual-recombinase lineage tracing, we demonstrated that MEOX1 knockdown enables highly efficient in vivo MF-to-iCM conversion, leading to significant reductions in cardiac fibrosis and substantial improvement in cardiac function after MI. Conclusions: Our study identifies the pathological upregulation of MEOX1 as a key mechanism underlying the reprogramming resistance of post-MI MFs, in both mouse and human. Overcoming this barrier achieves unprecedented, lineage-confirmed in vivo reprogramming efficiency, thereby addressing a significant obstacle for the clinical translation of in situ reprogramming therapies. Data included in this Series comprise the original bulk RNA-seq datasets of MGTM-reprogrammed mouse cardiac fibroblasts with control or Meox1 knockdown and with control vector/GFP or MEOX1 overexpression; RNA-seq datasets from human iPSCs, iPSC-derived cardiac fibroblasts, and iPSC-derived myofibroblasts; scRNA-seq datasets from MGTM-induced iCM cultures and normal or day-3 post-MI mouse hearts; MEOX1 CUT&Tag data; and the newly added three-biological-replicate bulk RNA-seq dataset comparing MGTM + shCtrl with MGTM + shMeox1 used for the revised manuscript.

observations.title: Overcoming Intrinsic Barriers in Myofibroblasts Permits Efficient Cardiac Reprogramming Post-Infarction

metadata.summary: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) commonly coexists with atrial fibrillation (AF), but shared mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, we hypothesized that Pitx2, a transcription factor located near the strongest genetic locus associated with AF in humans, increases susceptibility to HFpEF-like remodeling. We also sought to understand pathways that might be central to this increased risk. Male and female Pitx2+/− mice and wild-type littermates received 3-week subcutaneous osmotic pump infusion of saline or angiotensin II (Ang II; 500 ng/kg/min). Cardiac structure and function were assessed by echocardiography and catheterization, and functional capacity by exercise treadmill. RNA transcriptomic profiling was performed to identify candidate pathways. In a separate cohort, Ang II–treated mice were randomized to oral GKT136901 (30 mg/kg/day) or vehicle during infusion. After Ang II infusion, Pitx2+/− mice developed exaggerated HFpEF-like changes, including greater left ventricular hypertrophy, left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, and reduced treadmill performance. RNA-seq showed enrichment of metabolic and stress-response pathways with selective upregulation of Nox4, confirmed by RT-qPCR. GKT136901 attenuated structural remodeling, diastolic dysfunction indices, elevated filling pressures, and cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, but did not improve endurance. These findings implicate redox signaling, including Nox4, in AF genetic susceptibility–HFpEF interactions.

observations.title: Nox4 Mediates Diastolic Function in a Genetic Model of Pitx2 Haploinsufficiency

observations.text: During sleep, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) flow is enhanced and thought to facilitate clearance of metabolic waste from the brain. Human imaging has shown that sleep is associated with large waves of bulk CSF flow in the fourth ventricle; however, the CSF flow dynamics around brain tissue are unknown. Here, we investigated how CSF flow is organized across the subarachnoid space, a key site both for fluid exchange across cortical surface and for transport out of the cranium. We used an MRI technology at 7 Tesla that simultaneously measures cortical hemodynamics and slow subarachnoid CSF flow and applied this during sleep. We found that spontaneous infraslow hemodynamic oscillations were coupled to spatially structured, directional CSF flow throughout both ventricular and subarachnoid compartments. Hemodynamic oscillations and fourth-ventricle bulk flow were both associated with brain-wide CSF flow at different phases, indicating that they reflect a single coordinated CSF movement cycle. Compared to cardiac pulsations, a canonical driver of CSF movement, hemodynamic-driven CSF flow showed a distinct directional pattern and was smaller in instantaneous amplitude but produced substantially greater cumulative displacement and thus greater potential for transport within an oscillation period. Together, these findings show that hemodynamic oscillations during sleep are coupled to temporally coordinated and directional CSF flow throughout the ventricles and subarachnoid space, suggesting that sleep-dependent neuronal activity drives fluid movement across the human brain in a distinct spatial pattern.
observations.title: Spontaneous Hemodynamic Oscillations during Sleep Coordinate Directional CSF Flow in the Subarachnoid Space and Ventricles

metadata.summary: Oncofetal programs are often co-opted in high-grade gliomas and represent tumor cell vulnerabilities for therapeutic exploitation. Here, we integrate single nucleus RNA-seq and single-cell ATAC sequencing data generated from germinal matrix and cortical plate regions macrodissected from prenatal and postnatal developing brain autopsy tissue, creating an expanded spatiotemporal multi-omic dataset of gliogenic progenitors. The integrated multi-omics data includes previously published data (Ramos et al, Nature Commun 2022; Herring et al, Cell 2022) as well as newly-generated and herein deposited data. We use this dataset to interrogate oncofetal cell state composition in grade 4 gliomas across several published high-grade glioma / glioblastoma (GBM) datasets to uniquely assess tumor heterogeneity related to infiltrative biology near the margin and disease recurrence, in addition to genomic drivers. Our analyses reveal the preferential enrichment of glial intermediate progenitor cell (gIPC)-like cell state in GBM, most reminiscent of third-trimester germinal matrix gIPC progenitors, across tumor regions and in recurrence, irrespective of EGFR amplification status.

observations.text:
BackgroundCardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome encompasses interconnected diseases that share pathophysiological mechanisms, including microvascular dysfunction. Although rubidium-82 positron emission tomography/computed tomography ({superscript 2}Rb-PET/CT) is routinely used for myocardial perfusion imaging, its potential for integrated cardio-renal perfusion assessment and broader CKM phenotyping remains underexplored. We recently developed a compartment modelling approach to quantify renal perfusion from existing routine cardiac 82Rb-PET/CT scans, enabling simultaneous assessment of myocardial and kidney perfusion. However, real-world registries integrating these phenotypes with clinical outcomes are lacking.

AimTo establish a registry integrating 82Rb-PET-derived myocardial and renal perfusion, CT-derived CKM imaging biomarkers, and detailed clinical and outcome data.

MethodsThe APOLLO registry is a single-centre, retrospective database comprising approximately 1,200 consecutive patients who underwent myocardial perfusion imaging with 82Rb-PET/CT at Alrijne Hospital (Leiderdorp, the Netherlands) between 2021-2023. Clinical, laboratory, medication, echocardiographic, and imaging data were retrospectively collected. Myocardial perfusion was quantified using myocardial blood flow and myocardial flow reserve, and renal perfusion using renal blood flow and effective renal plasma flow. Additional CT-derived biomarkers included measures of adiposity and frailty, great vessel diameters, and vascular calcification. Echocardiographic diastolic dysfunction grade, H2FPEF score, CKM stage, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were also collected.

ConclusionThe APOLLO registry integrates {superscript 2}Rb-PET-derived myocardial and renal perfusion measurements with CT-derived CKM imaging biomarkers and clinical outcomes. This enables investigation of cardio-renal perfusion and their associations with CKM phenotypes and cardiovascular outcomes.
observations.title: Design and Rationale of the APOLLO Registry: Integrated Assessment of Cardio-Renal Perfusion and Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Phenotyping Using 82Rb-PET/CT

metadata.summary: Degenerative mitral valve disease (DMVD) is a highly prevalent cardiac condition characterized by mitral valve interstitial cell (MVIC) activation and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. To investigate the transcriptional reprogramming underlying these processes, we performed RNA sequencing on an established three-dimensional (3D) porcine MVIC-collagen (VIC-COL) model.Following a 14-day maturation period, the constructs were treated with transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) for an additional 14 days, while untreated constructs cultured for the same duration served as controls. Samples were prepared from cells derived from three independent biological replicates (i.e. mitral valves from three different pigs). For each replicate, three constructs were pooled as one sample for final analysis. The analysis identified 915 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), revealing a significant transcriptional shift. Specifically, TGF-β1 led to a predominant upregulation of immune and inflammatory networks, including the IL-6/JAK/STAT3, TNF-α/NF-κB, and NOD-like receptor pathways, alongside processes associated with extracellular matrix organization, cell-cell adhesion, cell adhesion regulation, and cellular senescence. Furthermore, cross-species transcriptomic comparisons with a clinical canine DMVD dataset confirmed the conservation of these immune-centric signatures. Collectively, our findings suggest that immune-inflammatory signaling may act as a key modulator of ECM remodeling associated with MVIC activation. Moreover, the 3D VIC-COL system established in this study can serve as a reliable in vitro platform for investigating MVIC activation, ECM remodeling, and immune-related pathway changes in DMVD pathogenesis.

observations.text: Which experiences persist as memories is a fundamental question in neurobiology. The balance between memory persistence and suppression is thought to be optimal for an organism to adapt to the ever-changing environment. Memory suppression is a process by which the brain limits the strength and expression of memories. Memory suppressors are genes whose disruption can enhance memory at different stages: acquisition, consolidation, forgetting, or recall. Here, using aversive classical conditioning in Drosophila, we show that Gq acts as a memory suppressor in PPL1 dopaminergic neurons. Knockdown of gq in dopaminergic neurons enhances acquisition, strengthens anesthesia-resistant memory, and impairs reversal learning. In vivo functional imaging revealed that gq knockdown amplifies shock-evoked responses in a type of PPL1 neuron. Additionally, using ex vivo imaging and pharmacological experiments, we reveal that both Gq and the OAMB receptor alter octopamine-evoked ER calcium responses in PPL1 neurons. Our results uncover a new role of Gq signaling within dopaminergic neurons that suppresses memory.
observations.title: A gαq signaling pathway in dopaminergic neurons suppresses memory

observations.text: Super-enhancers (SEs) drive cell-identity gene expression, yet their identification relies on epigenomic profiling (e.g., H3K27ac ChIP-seq), precluding discovery in unprofiled cellular states and leaving their underlying sequence grammar unknown. Here, we present Borzoi-SE, a deep learning framework built upon the genomic transformer Borzoi that formulates SE discovery as hierarchical, cell-type-resolved genomic object detection directly from long-range sequence across 90 human lineages. Base-resolution attribution recovers lineage-defining master transcription factors across cell types. Within SEs shared across lineages, it reveals lineage-dependent motif usage, suggesting that the same regulatory regions can support distinct cell-type-specific programs. Using in silico ablation, Borzoi-SE decoded the functional hierarchy of the {beta}-globin super-enhancer, prioritizing hypersensitive site 2 (HS2) as the dominant constituent, which we experimentally verified via CRISPR interference. Trained without variant-effect labels, Borzoi-SE identified gain-of-super-enhancer variants in different tissues. At the CHRM2 locus, a single-nucleotide variant created a de novo glucocorticoid receptor (GR) motif that recruited activated GR and potentiated adjacent MEF2 regulatory syntax, nucleating a cardiac super-enhancer. Orthogonal multi-omics and population-genetic evidence linked this variant to increased CHRM2 expression and variation in resting heart rate and PR-interval duration. Borzoi-SE establishes a general framework for decoding SE regulatory grammar and prioritizing causal non-coding variants directly from sequence.
observations.title: Decoding super-enhancer regulatory grammar and pathogenic gain-of-function variants directly from DNA sequence

observations.text: Ageing is associated with reduced skeletal muscle mass and function. Testosterone, the main androgenic hormone, exerts its anabolic effects in muscle through androgen receptor (AR) mediated pathways, with evidence suggesting that AR availability may represent a rate-limiting factor in androgen signalling. Rodent studies report age-related reductions in AR expression, however findings in human muscle are inconclusive. This study aimed to characterise age-related changes in AR expression and its upstream and downstream regulators in human skeletal muscle. To this end, we developed a novel R-based pipeline, MetAR, for reproducible meta-analyses of publicly available RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) datasets, to investigate associations between target gene expression and variables of interest. Eligible datasets included skeletal muscle samples from healthy adult males aged [≥]18 years, with an age range of [≥] 10 years and sample size [≥] 6. Raw counts data were downloaded, appraised and trimmed mean of M-values (TMM) normalised. Dataset-level associations between age and target gene expression were modelled and random-effects meta-analyses performed. Sixteen RNA-seq datasets (n = 364; age 18-92 years) were included. AR expression was negatively associated with age ({beta} = -0.006 log2 TMM-Counts Per Million (CPM) per year, p < 0.001, 4.4% decline per decade, I-squared=53.8%, 95% prediction interval [-0.0143 to +0.0014]). Age was associated with a reduction in expression of regulators of AR stability, transcriptional activity and nuclear transport, as well as downstream regulators relevant to AR signalling. These findings suggest multi-faceted age-associated remodelling of AR expression, signalling and nuclear transport, potentially explaining a component of age-associated muscle loss.
observations.title: MetAR: A semi-automated meta-analysis of skeletal muscle androgen receptors association with age

observations.text: Neuronal activation drives activity-dependent gene expression that underlies experience-associated synaptic modifications, learning and memory. Here we show that the histone variant CENP-A, best known for specifying centromere identity, is dynamically regulated by synaptic activity at both the RNA and protein levels in postmitotic neurons. Neuronal activation increases a non-centromeric nuclear pool of CENP-A while leaving centromeric CENP-A levels unchanged. Downregulation of CENP-A selectively reduces the activity-associated non-centromeric pool, impairs activity-dependent induction of immediate-early genes such as FOS and ARC, and disrupts hippocampus-dependent learning and memory. Furthermore, we find that activity-dependent neuronal responses in human embryonic stem cell-derived forebrain organoids similarly require CENP-A. Our results reveal a mitosis-independent, conserved role of CENP-A for driving plasticity in mammalian neurons.
observations.title: Co-option of CENP-A for activity-induced neuronal plasticity
